title: Python streaming chat: session adapter, event contracts, retry playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a developer-friendly session adapter for Python SDK streaming chat that normalizes event contracts, emits explicit lifecycle signals, and provides deterministic retry semantics. Deliver examples and a playbook that guides engineers integrating streaming completions into production services with backpressure and idempotent retries.
background: Customers and internal teams report two recurring integration pain points: 1) ambiguous event shapes across SDK layers (partial content vs control signals), and 2) brittle retry behavior when networks drop mid-stream. Current helpers are fragmented: callback sinks, async iterators, and ad-hoc resume logic live in different modules. This leads to inconsistent telemetry and repeated engineering time when onboarding streaming into services.
proposal: Add a compact SessionAdapter abstraction that sits between the transport (http/sse/websocket) and application consumer. The adapter will: 1) normalize raw events into a small, typed set of event kinds (CONTENT_DELTA, METADATA, KEEPALIVE, END, ERROR, CHECKPOINT), 2) expose a single async iterator API plus optional callback hooks, 3) surface retryable checkpoints with idempotency keys, and 4) emit backpressure signals that map to underlying queue/timer policies. Provide a playbook doc and three canonical examples: (A) web request handler that proxies stream to client, (B) worker that aggregates partials into convo chunks with checkpointed persistence, (C) CLI demo that shows resume on transient failure.
api_surface:
SessionAdapter(api: Transport, *, resume_store: Optional[ResumeStore]=None, batch_policy: str='auto') -> object

Primary methods/attributes:
- async for event in adapter.stream(session_id=str): yields Event objects with attributes (kind, token, sequence, checkpoint_id, meta)
- adapter.on_event(fn): optional sync/async callback invoked for every normalized Event
- adapter.checkpoint(checkpoint_id): application-visible hook to mark persisted progress
- adapter.resume_from(checkpoint_id): instruct adapter to request model prefix/KV resume if supported
- adapter.shutdown(signal='graceful'): flushes inflight and emits END or ERROR event

Event kinds: [CONTENT_DELTA, METADATA, KEEPALIVE, END, ERROR, CHECKPOINT]

Retry semantics (summary):
- Transient transport failures: adapter attempts up to N attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (configurable). If a checkpoint exists, adapter resumes from checkpoint by re-requesting model with resume_token and replays any cached deltas where necessary.
- Non-retryable model errors propagate as ERROR event with code and suggestion.
- Idempotency: session_id + checkpoint_id form the client-visible idempotency key; SDK will surface a stable header X-Redwood-Resume-Id when resuming.

Config knobs: retry_policy, max_retries, checkpoint_interval_tokens, batch_policy, telemetry_context
examples:
1) Minimal async iterator usage:

from redwood.sdk.streaming import SessionAdapter

adapter = SessionAdapter(transport=HttpStreamTransport())
async for ev in adapter.stream(session_id='u-123'):
    if ev.kind == 'CONTENT_DELTA':
        print(ev.token, end='')
    elif ev.kind == 'CHECKPOINT':
        await store.save(ev.checkpoint_id, ev.sequence)
    elif ev.kind == 'END':
        break

2) Callback + backpressure demo:

async def sink(ev):
    await db.write_partial(ev.sequence, ev.token)
    if should_backpressure():
        await adapter.pause()  # polite signal to transport pool

adapter.on_event(sink)
await adapter.start(session_id='u-123')

3) Resume example after transient network drop:

# adapter persisted last checkpoint cp-42
adapter = SessionAdapter(transport=HttpStreamTransport(), resume_store=LocalResumeStore())
adapter.resume_from('cp-42')
async for ev in adapter.stream(session_id='u-123'):
    # adapter will re-request model with resume token header and skip already-applied tokens
    pass
migration_notes:
- Existing consumers using raw event dicts should switch to adapter.stream() and pattern-match Event.kind instead of event['type']. A small shim adapter.from_raw_events(...) is provided for quick migration.
- Rename previous helper modules: old module streaming.consumer -> streaming.legacy_consumer (deprecated).
- Document recommended default checkpoint interval (every 512 tokens or on logical turn boundary).
acceptance_criteria:
1) SessionAdapter implemented in SDK with tests covering: normalization of all Event kinds, checkpoint emission, resume behavior, and retry backoff.
2) End-to-end example apps (web proxy, worker aggregator, CLI resume) in examples/streaming/ that run in CI smoke test (ci/streaming-smoke).
3) Telemetry emitted for: event rate, checkpoint frequency, retry attempts, resume success/failure, and end-to-end latency.
4) Migration guide added to docs and PR reviewed by DevExp and API owners.
5) Benchmarks show no more than 5% added latency in happy-path relative to current minimal iterator helper.

notes:
Design considerations: keep Event small and serializable for cross-process handoff; avoid including full token buffers in telemetry by default. We chose explicit CHECKPOINT events instead of implicit byte offsets to allow customer-defined persistence semantics. Backpressure will be a best-effort signal and cannot guarantee upstream pause on every transport; examples will show how to implement polite yield-based drains.

Open questions:
- Should adapter expose a high-level `reassemble_text()` helper or leave assembly to consumers? (proposal: provide optional helper but not default to avoid surprising memory use)
- Default checkpoint interval: 512 tokens vs 1 turn boundary -- set to 512 for now and add a heuristic to prefer turn boundaries when detected.
